questions.question:
In the sentence

"Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos, content creators must a labyrinthine ecosystem encompassing algorithmic unpredictability..."

What is the function of the introductory phrase "Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos"?

options.text: Prepositional phrase functioning as a noun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: Adverbial phrase modifying "navigate"***

 
 
• The phrase "Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos" is a **prepositional phrase** (headed by the preposition "beyond").
 
• When a prepositional phrase starts a sentence and provides the "setting" or "circumstance" for the main action, it functions as an **adverbial modifier**.
 
• It specifically modifies the verb **"navigate,"** describing the metaphorical location or scope within which the creators must act.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Appositive phrase***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. An appositive is a noun phrase that renames a noun right next to it (e.g., "The platform, **a digital giant**..."). This phrase does not rename "content creators."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Prepositional phrase functioning as a noun***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A phrase functions as a noun when it serves as the subject or object. Here, it is modifying the action, not acting as a "thing."
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Absolute phrase with implied verb***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. An absolute phrase modifies the entire sentence and must contain a noun and a participle (e.g., "The glitz having faded, the work began"). This phrase lacks that structure.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverbial Functions**: Introductory phrases that answer "Where?", "When?", "Why?", or "To what extent?" are usually adverbial. This phrase answers "Where" (metaphorically) the navigation occurs.
 
• **Labyrinthine**: This adjective refers to something like a labyrinth—highly complex and confusing. It supports the author's argument that YouTube is a difficult "ecosystem" to master.
 
• **Punctuation Tip**: When an introductory adverbial phrase is long (usually four words or more), a comma is used after it to help the reader distinguish it from the main subject of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Who tore the window curtains ?

options.text: By whom were the window curtains torn ?
By whom are the window curtains torn?
By whom were the window curtains tore?
By whom were the window curtains teared?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Structure for "Who":** In passive voice, interrogative sentences starting with "Who" are replaced by "By whom."
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The sentence "Who tore the window curtains?" is in the **Simple Past Tense** (Subject + $V_2$ + Object).
 
• **Passive Voice Formula (Simple Past Interrogative):** By whom + was/were + object + $V_3$ (past participle)?
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Since the object "the window curtains" is plural, the auxiliary verb "were" is used.
 
• **Verb Form:** The three forms of the verb are tear ($V_1$), tore ($V_2$), and **torn ($V_3$)**. Passive voice always uses the $V_3$ form.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"By whom were the window curtains torn?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"By whom are the window curtains torn?" – Incorrect because "are" is used for the present tense.
 
• **Option 3: **"By whom were the window curtains tore?" – Incorrect because "tore" is the $V_2$ form; passive voice requires the $V_3$ form (torn).
 
• **Option 4: **"By whom were the window curtains teared?" – Incorrect because "teared" is not a valid word in this context; "tear" is an irregular verb.

questions.question:
Select the correct Passive form of the given sentence.

When will the manager attend the programme?

options.text: When will the programme be attended by the manager?
When would the programme be attended by the manager?
When can the programme be attended by the manager?
When should the programme be attended by the manager?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active sentence "When will the manager attend the programme?" is in the **Future Simple Tense**.
 
• **Passive Voice Structure (Interrogative):** For questions starting with "When" in the future simple tense, the structure is: *When + will + Object + be + $V_3$ + by + Subject?*
 
• **Object and Subject:** The object "the programme" becomes the new subject, and the original subject "the manager" moves to the end after the preposition "by."
 
• **Modal Consistency:** In voice conversion (unlike direct/indirect speech), the modal verb "will" does not change to "would," "can," or "should." It remains "will."
 
• **Verb Form:** The base verb "attend" ($V_1$) changes to its past participle form, **"attended"** ($V_3$).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When will the programme be attended by the manager?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"When would..." is incorrect because it changes the modal verb from "will" to "would," which is typically done in Narration (Direct/Indirect speech), not Voice.
 
• **Option 3: **"When can..." is incorrect because it changes the meaning/possibility by using "can."
 
• **Option 4: **"When should..." is incorrect because it changes the sense of the sentence to an obligation or suggestion.

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said to his brother, "Please stop playing loud music."
 
• **Sentence Type:** This is an **Imperative Sentence** expressing a request (indicated by the word "Please").
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:** In imperative sentences containing a request, the reporting verb "said to" is changed into **requested** or **asked**.
 
• **Omission of "Please":** The word "Please" is removed in indirect speech because the reporting verb ("requested") already conveys the polite nature of the sentence.
 
• **Conjunction/Infinitive:** Imperative sentences do not use "that." Instead, the verb in the reported speech is converted into an **infinitive** (to + verb). Here, "stop" becomes **"to stop"**.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence ends with a full stop.

**Correct Sentence:** *He requested his brother to stop playing loud music.*
